nodes.summary: The one-state Büchi automaton for `G φ` with `φ` propositional: it stays forever, requiring every letter to satisfy `φ`.
nodes.title: One-state Büchi automaton for always φ

nodes.summary: A letter is a set $s$ of atoms (the atoms true at it). A propositional formula is evaluated at $s$ by recursion: an atom $a$ is true iff $a \in s$, truth $\top$ is true, $\neg\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is not, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is true iff both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are true.
nodes.title: Evaluating a propositional formula at a letter

nodes.summary: Take as letters the sets of atoms, an atom $a$ holding at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. For every formula $\psi$ of the restricted safety fragment there is a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states whose ω-language is exactly the set of infinite words satisfying $\psi$, read as an LTL formula.
nodes.title: Büchi automata for the restricted safety fragment

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The two-state Büchi automaton for “infinitely often $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at infinitely many positions.
nodes.title: The infinitely-often automaton recognizes G F φ

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the one-state Büchi automaton for $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters (sets of atoms) that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$.
nodes.title: The always automaton recognizes G φ

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The two-state Büchi automaton for “eventually always $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at all but finitely many…
nodes.title: The eventually-always automaton recognizes F G φ

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the three-state Büchi automaton for $\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters (sets of atoms) that satisfy $\varphi$ read as an LTL formula, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$.
nodes.title: The propositional automaton recognizes φ

nodes.summary: For a Büchi automaton $A$ over letters that are sets of atoms, the shift automaton of $A$ accepts an infinite word $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ iff $A$ accepts its tail $x_1 x_2 x_3 \ldots$.
nodes.title: The shift automaton reads the tail

nodes.summary: The propositional formulas over a set of atoms are generated by the atoms, the constant truth $\top$, negation $\neg\varphi$ and conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, this Büchi automaton over letters that are sets of atoms has a start state $u$ and two verdict states $t$ and $f$, of which only $t$ is accepting. From $u$, on a letter $s$ it moves to $t$ if $\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ and to $f$ otherwise; from $t$ and from $f$ it stays in the same state on every letter. So it records the verdict of $\varphi$ on the first letter.
nodes.title: Büchi automaton for a propositional formula

nodes.summary: The safety formulas over a type of atoms are generated by the following rules: every propositional formula $\varphi$ is a safety formula; if $\psi$ and $\rho$ are safety formulas, then so are $\psi \wedge \rho$, $\psi \vee \rho$ and $X\,\psi$ (next $\psi$); and for every propositional formula $\varphi$, $G\,\varphi$ (always $\varphi$) is a safety formula.
nodes.title: The restricted safety fragment of LTL

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula, let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms, and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that letter, the LTL translation of $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the letter $w_k$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the current letter

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that letter, $w$ satisfies the LTL translation of $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the first letter $w_0$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the first letter

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Büchi automaton over the alphabet of sets of atoms. Its shift is the Büchi automaton whose states are the states of $A$ together with one new state $\bot$, whose only start state is $\bot$, and whose accepting states are the accepting states of $A$. Its transitions are exactly the following: on every letter, from $\bot$ to each start state of $A$; and on a letter $x$, from a state $q$ of $A$ to a state…
nodes.title: The shift of a Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: The translation of propositional formulas into LTL formulas is defined by recursion: an atom $a$ goes to the LTL atom $a$, truth goes to the LTL truth constant $\top$, $\neg\varphi$ goes to the LTL negation of the translation of $\varphi$, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ goes to the LTL conjunction of the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas as LTL formulas

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
